operator.name: Team Operator
operator.one_sentence: Configures world difficulty, rover sensor variant, and waypoint tour inside the Mission Control interface.

mission_gui.name: Mission Control GUI
mission_gui.one_sentence: Orchestrates grid-to-metric coordinate injection, readiness-gated terminal launches, 20-minute batch watchdogs, and master HTML report compilation.

gazebo_sim.name: Gazebo Harmonic
gazebo_sim.one_sentence: Runs rigid-body Marsyard physics, 6-wheel rocker-bogie dynamics, 7 link contact sensors, 100 Hz BNO055 IMU, and 5 Hz ZED2i RGB-D rendering.

ros2_control.name: ros2_control DiffDrive
ros2_control.one_sentence: Chains joint_state_broadcaster, 6-wheel diff_drive_controller (enable_odom_tf: false), and arm_controller 12s after entity spawn.

ros_gz_bridge.name: ROS ↔ Gazebo Bridge
ros_gz_bridge.one_sentence: Bridges /clock, /bno055/data, /zed2i/image_raw, /zed2i/depth, /world/rover_world/pose/info, and 7 link contact streams into ROS 2.

zed_deg.name: ZED2i Degradation
zed_deg.one_sentence: Projects 3D sun coordinates into camera pixels to inject solar glare, Mars dust, and 0.003·Z² stereo noise before unprojecting XYZRGB PointCloud2.

encoder_sim.name: Encoder Simulator
encoder_sim.one_sentence: Quantizes continuous left/right middle-wheel joint angles into integer pulse counts (201,554 pulses/rev) on /joint_states_updated.

lidar_cluster.name: LiDAR Cluster Node
lidar_cluster.one_sentence: Executes Open3D CUDA ROI cropping, 6cm voxel downsampling, SOR/ROR denoising, ≤45° slope-aware RANSAC, PCA roughness, and DBSCAN clustering.

aruco_node.name: ArUco Detector Node
aruco_node.one_sentence: Designed to compute 6-DOF IPPE-Square marker poses on /zed2i/image_raw_updated; isolated OS process exits on active_mapping_msgs ImportError at startup.

obstacle_pub.name: Obstacle Publisher
obstacle_pub.one_sentence: Transforms camera-frame 3D bounding boxes into odom via TF2, merges repeat sightings with EMA (α=0.35), and prunes stale rocks after 4s.

bev_vis.name: BEV & Perception Eval
bev_vis.one_sentence: Renders top-down bird's-eye-view debug imagery and evaluates 3D bounding-box IoU against obstacle_data.npy ground truth.

gt_bridge.name: Ground Truth Bridge
gt_bridge.one_sentence: Extracts child_frame_id 'roar_rover' from /world/rover_world/pose/info and republishes 50 Hz PoseWithCovarianceStamped on /zed2i/zed_node/pose_with_covariance.

ieskf_loc.name: IESKF Localization
ieskf_loc.one_sentence: Fuses 100 Hz BNO055 IMU (-90° yaw fix), encoder pulses (WIO), and visual pose using Sugeno WO-FIS/VO-FIS and 4-gate ZUPT to broadcast /odom and TF.

terrain_map.name: Terrain Mapping
terrain_map.one_sentence: Seeds a 100×100m 2.5D grid from heightmap_mars_yard.npz and stamps Kalman-verified boulders (variance < 0.025 m²) onto /active_map/heightmap.

costmap_fuser.name: Unified Costmap Fuser
costmap_fuser.one_sentence: Computes Sobel slope, Laplacian roughness (0–99), >0.45m lethal cliff masks (100), and L2 safety inflation onto /unified_costmap (TRANSIENT_LOCAL).

nav2_lifecycle.name: Nav2 Lifecycle Mgr
nav2_lifecycle.one_sentence: Autostarts and transitions map_server, planner_server, controller_server, behavior_server, and bt_navigator into ACTIVE state.

bt_navigator.name: BT Navigator Server
bt_navigator.one_sentence: Hosts the /navigate_to_pose action server and ticks navigate_to_pose_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml at 100 Hz.

dstar_planner.name: D* Lite Planner
dstar_planner.one_sentence: Runs 5m BFS goal snapping, backward D* Lite with Dijkstra obstacle clearance + squared terrain cost, incremental km_ repair, and 3-pass smoothing.

mppi_ctrl.name: MPPI Controller
mppi_ctrl.one_sentence: Evaluates 2,000 DiffDrive rollouts (56 steps, 8 critics) at 20 Hz on an 8×8m rolling local costmap and remaps TwistStamped directly to /diff_drive_controller/cmd_vel.

wp_follower.name: Waypoint Follower
wp_follower.one_sentence: Parses metric YAML targets, appends Start (0,0) as Leg 5, and dispatches sequential /navigate_to_pose goals until STATUS_SUCCEEDED.

collision_mon.name: Collision Monitor
collision_mon.one_sentence: Subscribes to 7 per-link Gazebo contact streams via contact_bridge, whitelisting safe pebble meshes {5..9} in obstacle_data.npy and flagging boulder hits.

referee_core.name: Referee Core Engine
referee_core.one_sentence: Runs a 10 Hz audit loop over /odom, /clock, and /rover/collision_flag to enforce KILL/TIMEOUT rules, verify settled stops, and compute 300-point ERC scores.

report_gen.name: Report & Eval Suite
report_gen.one_sentence: Writes ERC_Report_Live.html, timestamped final ERC scorecards, and parallel SLAM RMSE & Perception IoU benchmark dashboards.

events.title: Sun Projection, Glare Holes, Dust & XYZRGB Unprojection

events.title: Stage 4a: Iterative Slope-Aware RANSAC (≤45°)

            return

        if elapsed >= self.SIM_READY_TIMEOUT_S:

        QTimer.singleShot(

    def _batch_launch_nav(self, generation):

        nav_cmd = (f"cd {self.ws_root} && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && " \
                   f"source install/setup.bash && " \
                   f"ros2 launch navstack_nav2 roar_nav2_only.launch.py "

        self._open_in_terminal(nav_cmd, f"BATCH NAV2: {ctx['mission_id']}", keep_open=False)

        self._nav_ready = False
        self._batch_wait_for_nav_ready(generation, elapsed=0)

    def _check_nav_ready_worker(self):
        try:
            cmd = "source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && ros2 action list"
            result = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", cmd], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=1.5)
            self._nav_ready = ("/navigate_to_pose" in result.stdout)
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _batch_wait_for_nav_ready(self, generation, elapsed):
        if generation != self._batch_generation:
            return  # item was aborted/skipped while waiting

        if self._nav_ready:
            self._batch_launch_referee_and_waypoints(generation)
            return

        if elapsed >= self.NAV_READY_TIMEOUT_S:
            self._batch_abort_item("nav2 never became ready")
            return

        threading.Thread(target=self._check_nav_ready_worker, daemon=True).start()
        QTimer.singleShot(
            self.BATCH_READY_POLL_MS,
            lambda: self._batch_wait_for_nav_ready(generation, elapsed + self.BATCH_READY_POLL_MS / 1000)
        )

    def _batch_launch_referee_and_waypoints(self, generation):
        if generation != self._batch_generation:
            return

        ctx = self._batch_item_ctx
        mission_id = ctx["mission_id"]

            f"source install/setup.bash && " \
            f"ros2 launch referee_engine roar_full_evaluation.launch.py "
            f"mission:={mission_id} world_num:={ctx['world_num']} run_mock:=false "
            f"enable_slam:={ctx.get('slam_val', 'false')} enable_perception:={ctx.get('perc_val', 'true')} enable_pursuit:={ctx.get('pursuit_val', 'true')}"
        )
        self._open_in_terminal(referee_cmd, f"BATCH REFEREE: {mission_id}", keep_open=False)

        # 4. Send waypoints — same follower invocation as the "3. SEND WPTS" button,
        # with the same graceful teardown, tracked so we know when the item is done.
        kills = "pkill -2 -f ros2; pkill -2 -f gz; pkill -2 -f ruby; pkill -2 -f rviz2; pkill -2 -f nav2"
        wp_cmd = (\
            f"cd {self.ws_root} && source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && " \
            f"source install/setup.bash && " \
            f"python3 {self.nav_ws}/path-planning/globalPlanner/scripts/batch_waypoint_follower.py --params {self.yaml_path} ; "
            f"echo 'Waypoints finished. Tearing down batch item...' ; sleep 2 ; {kills}"
        )

        self.batch_process = QProcess(self)
        self.batch_process.finished.connect(lambda: self._on_batch_process_finished(generation))
        self.batch_process.start("gnome-terminal", ["--wait", "--title", f"BATCH WPTS: {mission_id}", "--", "bash", "-c", wp_cmd])

    def _on_batch_process_finished(self, generation):
        if generation != self._batch_generation:
            return  # stale — this item was already aborted/skipped
        self.batch_timeout_timer.stop()
        self._compile_master_report(self.current_gui_mission)
        self.completed_batch_count += 1
        self.kill_all_nodes(show_msg=False) # Guarantee all leftover terminals and nodes are wiped!
        self._process_next_batch_item()

    def listener_callback(self, msg: PointCloud2):
        # Read all params fresh each call → ros2 param set takes effect live
        p = self._read_params()

        # ── Stage 0: GPU-accelerated ROI distance mask ───────────────────
        points, colors = self._pc2_to_numpy_rgb(msg)
        if points.shape[0] == 0:
            return

        if self._use_gpu:
            # Upload to GPU, compute squared norms, threshold, download mask
            pts_t  = o3c.Tensor(points, dtype=o3c.float32, device=self._gpu_device)
            sq     = (pts_t * pts_t).sum(1)                     # Nx1 squared distances
            mask_t = sq < float(p['max_dist'] ** 2)             # boolean mask on GPU
            mask   = mask_t.cpu().numpy().astype(bool)
        else:
            mask = np.linalg.norm(points, axis=1) < p['max_dist']

        points = points[mask]
        colors = colors[mask]
        if points.shape[0] == 0:
            return

        # Wrap in Open3D legacy PointCloud for the rest of the pipeline
        pcd = o3d.geometry.PointCloud()
        pcd.points = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(points)
        pcd.colors = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(colors)

        # ── Stage 1: Voxel-grid downsampling ────────────────────────────
        pcd = pcd.voxel_down_sample(voxel_size=p['voxel_size'])
        if len(pcd.points) < 10:
            return

        # ── Stage 2: Statistical Outlier Removal (SOR) ──────────────────
        # Removes per-point speckle by comparing each point's mean
        # neighbour distance to the global mean±σ across all points.
        if p['sor_en'] and len(pcd.points) >= p['sor_k']:
            pcd, _ = pcd.remove_statistical_outlier(
                nb_neighbors=int(p['sor_k']),
                std_ratio=float(p['sor_std'])
            )
            if len(pcd.points) < 5:
                return

        # ── Stage 3: Radius Outlier Removal (ROR) ───────────────────────
        # Removes isolated points (sensor reflections) that survive SOR.
        if p['ror_en'] and len(pcd.points) >= p['ror_n']:
            pcd, _ = pcd.remove_radius_outlier(
                nb_points=int(p['ror_n']),
                radius=float(p['ror_r'])
            )
            if len(pcd.points) < 5:
                return

        # Publish clean cloud (with ground, for debugging in RViz)
        self.filtered_pub.publish(self._pcd_to_pc2_rgb(pcd, msg.header))

        # ── Stage 4: Slope-aware iterative RANSAC plane removal ─────────
        # Strips ground + ramps while PRESERVING steep rock faces.
        pcd_ng = self._remove_planes_slope_aware(pcd, p)
        if pcd_ng is None or len(pcd_ng.points) == 0:
            return

        # ── Stage 4b: Surface-normal roughness filter ────────────────────
        # Removes any remaining smooth-slope points; keeps only rough/sharp rock points.
        if p['roughness_en']:
            pcd_ng = self._roughness_filter(pcd_ng, p)
            if pcd_ng is None or len(pcd_ng.points) < 5:
                return

        self.no_ground_pub.publish(self._pcd_to_pc2_rgb(pcd_ng, msg.header))

        # ── Stage 5: DBSCAN clustering ───────────────────────────────────
        # Groups surviving points into candidate obstacle clusters.
        labels = np.array(
            pcd_ng.cluster_dbscan(
                eps=p['cluster_tol'],
                min_points=p['min_cluster'],
                print_progress=False
            )
        )

        # Build message containers
        detections     = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        raw_detections = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        slam_detections = ObstacleDetectionArray(header=msg.header)

        max_label = int(labels.max()) if labels.size > 0 else -1

        for i in range(max_label + 1):
            idx = np.where(labels == i)[0]
            if len(idx) < p['min_cluster'] or len(idx) > p['max_cluster']:
                continue  # DBSCAN already filters by min, but max is our extra gate

            cluster_pcd = pcd_ng.select_by_index(idx)
            aabb   = cluster_pcd.get_axis_aligned_bounding_box()
            center = aabb.get_center()
            extent = aabb.get_extent()
            sx, sy, sz = float(extent[0]), float(extent[1]), float(extent[2])
            cx, cy, cz = float(center[0]), float(center[1]), float(center[2])

            # Assemble Detection3D (shared by raw + filtered arrays)
            det = self._make_detection3d(msg.header, center, extent, i)
            raw_detections.detections.append(det)

            # ── Stage 6: Bounding-box shape filter ──────────────────────
            if not (p['min_bx'] <= sx <= p['max_bx'] and
                    p['min_by'] <= sy <= p['max_by'] and
                    p['min_bz'] <= sz <= p['max_bz']):
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by bbox: x={sx:.2f} y={sy:.2f} z={sz:.2f}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Aspect-ratio filter (flat slab rejection) ───────
            # A ramp remnant is wide+deep but not tall.  Rocks are chunkier.
            if p['max_dr'] > 0 and sy > 1e-3 and (sz / sy) > p['max_dr']:
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by depth/height={sz/sy:.1f} > {p["max_dr"]}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Distance filter ─────────────────────────────────
            cl_dist = float(np.linalg.norm([cx, cy, cz]))
            if cl_dist < p['min_cdist'] or cl_dist > p['max_cdist']:
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Centre-height (Y-axis) filter ───────────────────
            # ZED Y=down; positive Y = below camera (on ground level).
            # Rocks sit near Y=0..+0.5; reject clusters above or far below.
            if cy < p['min_cy'] or cy > p['max_cy']:
                continue

            detections.detections.append(det)

            slam_obs = ObstacleDetection()
            slam_obs.position   = Point(x=cx, y=cy, z=cz)
            slam_obs.dimensions = Vector3(x=sx, y=sy, z=sz)
            slam_detections.detections.append(slam_obs)

        # Publish
        self.raw_cluster_pub.publish(raw_detections)
        self.cluster_pub.publish(detections)
        self.slam_pub.publish(slam_detections)
        self._publish_markers(detections, msg.header)

    def detect(self, image: np.ndarray):
        """Return (corners, ids, rejected) from the first dictionary that hits."""
        for d in self._DICTS:

            if self._use_new_api:
                det = cv2.aruco.ArucoDetector(adict, self._params)
                corners, ids, rejected = det.detectMarkers(image)

        """
        Returns rvecs, tvecs as lists (one entry per detected marker).
        Uses SOLVEPNP_IPPE_SQUARE — the most accurate method for square targets.
        """
        if not corners:
            return [], []
        half = marker_size / 2.0
        obj_pts = np.array([
            [-half,  half, 0.0],
            [ half,  half, 0.0],
            [ half, -half, 0.0],
            [-half, -half, 0.0],
        ], dtype=np.float32)

        rvecs, tvecs = [], []
        for corner in corners:
            ok, rvec, tvec = cv2.solvePnP(
                obj_pts,
                corner.reshape(-1, 2).astype(np.float32),
                K, dist,
                flags=cv2.SOLVEPNP_IPPE_SQUARE
            )
            if ok:
                rvecs.append(rvec)
                tvecs.append(tvec)
        return rvecs, tvecs

            dist_cam = math.sqrt(cx*cx + cy*cy + cz*cz)
            if dist_cam > self.get_parameter('max_detection_distance').value:
                continue

            # Transform obstacle centre to world frame
            pt_cam        = PointStamped()
            pt_cam.header = msg.header
            pt_cam.point  = det.bbox.center.position
            try:
                pt_world = tf2_geometry_msgs.do_transform_point(pt_cam, tf_stamped)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().warn(f'Transform failed: {e}')
                continue

            # Build world-frame detection
            out_det = Detection3D()
            out_det.header.frame_id       = world_frame
            out_det.header.stamp          = msg.header.stamp
            out_det.bbox.center.position.x = pt_world.point.x
            out_det.bbox.center.position.y = pt_world.point.y
            out_det.bbox.center.position.z = pt_world.point.z
            out_det.bbox.center.orientation.w = 1.0
            out_det.bbox.size.x = det.bbox.size.x
            out_det.bbox.size.y = det.bbox.size.y
            out_det.bbox.size.z = det.bbox.size.z
            hyp = ObjectHypothesisWithPose()
            hyp.hypothesis.class_id = class_id
            hyp.hypothesis.score    = score
            out_det.results.append(hyp)

            # Merge into obstacle map: if a known obstacle is within merge_radius, update it;
            # otherwise add a new entry
            merged = False
            for entry in self.obstacle_map.values():
                existing = entry['detection']
                dx = existing.bbox.center.position.x - pt_world.point.x
                dy = existing.bbox.center.position.y - pt_world.point.y
                dz = existing.bbox.center.position.z - pt_world.point.z
                if math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz) < merge_radius:
                    # Update in place with EMA (Exponential Moving Average) to eliminate jitter
                    existing.bbox.center.position.x = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.x + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.x
                    existing.bbox.center.position.y = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.y + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.y
                    existing.bbox.center.position.z = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.z + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.z
                    
                    existing.bbox.size.x = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.x + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.x
                    existing.bbox.size.y = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.y + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.y
                    existing.bbox.size.z = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.z + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.z
                    
                    # Keep highest confidence score
                    if out_det.results and existing.results:
                        existing.results[0].hypothesis.score = max(existing.results[0].hypothesis.score, out_det.results[0].hypothesis.score)

                    entry['last_seen']  = now
                    merged = True
                    break

            if not merged:
                if len(self.obstacle_map) >= self.get_parameter('max_obstacles').value:
                    # Map is full — drop the lowest-confidence entry to make room
                    oldest_key = min(
                        self.obstacle_map,
                        key=lambda k: self.obstacle_map[k]['detection'].results[0].hypothesis.score
                        if self.obstacle_map[k]['detection'].results else 0.0
                    )
                    del self.obstacle_map[oldest_key]

                self.obstacle_map[self._next_id] = {
                    'detection':  out_det,
                    'last_seen':  now,
                    'color_idx':  self._next_id,  # fixed forever — colour won't change
                }
                self._next_id += 1

        # Forget stale obstacles
        self._forget_old(now)

def _init_height_map(self):
        """Load the static height map from heightmap_file (.npz) or fall
        back to a flat zero map. The .npz's own grid/resolution/origin take
        priority over the map_* fallback parameters, since they describe the
        exact geometry the offline tool baked the map with."""
        loaded = self._load_npz(self._heightmap_file) if self._heightmap_file else None

        if loaded is not None:
            base = loaded
            self.get_logger().info(f"Loaded static height map from {self._heightmap_file}")
        else:
            if self._heightmap_file:
                self.get_logger().warn(
                    f"heightmap_file '{self._heightmap_file}' not found or invalid — using flat map."
                )
            base = np.zeros((self._rows, self._cols), dtype=np.float32)

        # The base map is the trusted prior (initial_height_variance) and is
        # immutable: verified obstacle tracks are stamped ON TOP of it into
        # self._height_map by _rebuild_height_map(), never blended into it.
        self._base_height_map = base
        # ArUco markers are a priori known landmarks, not live detections —
        # bake them into the trusted base itself (before it's ever copied)
        # so they survive every subsequent _rebuild_height_map() cycle.
        self._stamp_aruco_obstacles()
        self._height_map = self._base_height_map.copy()

    def _stamp_aruco_obstacles(self):
        """Stamp each ArUco marker's starting (x, y) cell into the base
        height map as a static obstacle, aruco_obstacle_height metres above
        whatever terrain height is already there. Markers are known ahead of
        time (unlike live detections), so they go straight into the trusted
        base rather than through the Kalman-tracked obstacle pipeline."""
        if not self._aruco_map_file:
            return

        if not os.path.isfile(self._aruco_map_file):
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f"aruco_map_file '{self._aruco_map_file}' not found — skipping marker obstacles."
            )
            return

        try:
            with open(self._aruco_map_file, "r") as f:
                data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            markers = data.get("markers", [])
        except Exception as exc:
            self.get_logger().warn(f"Failed to load aruco_map_file '{self._aruco_map_file}': {exc}")
            return

        stamped = 0
        for marker in markers:
            wx, wy, _wz = marker["position"]
            col = int((wx - self._origin_x) / self._resolution)
            row = int((wy - self._origin_y) / self._resolution)
            if not (0 <= row < self._rows and 0 <= col < self._cols):
                continue

            terrain = self._base_height_map[row, col]
            terrain_z = 0.0 if np.isnan(terrain) else float(terrain)
            self._base_height_map[row, col] = terrain_z + self._aruco_obstacle_height
            stamped += 1

        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Stamped {stamped}/{len(markers)} ArUco marker obstacles from "
            f"'{self._aruco_map_file}' (+{self._aruco_obstacle_height:.2f} m above terrain)"
        )

    def _load_npz(self, path: str) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            return None
        try:
            data = np.load(path)
            grid = np.asarray(data["grid"], dtype=np.float32)
        except Exception as exc:
            self.get_logger().warn(f"Failed to load heightmap_file '{path}': {exc}")
            return None

        self._rows, self._cols = grid.shape
        if "resolution" in data:
            self._resolution = float(data["resolution"])
        if "origin_x" in data:
            self._origin_x = float(data["origin_x"])
        if "origin_y" in data:
            self._origin_y = float(data["origin_y"])

        return grid

    # Odometry callback (stored for fallback transform when TF is not available)

    def _on_odom(self, msg: Odometry):
        self._latest_odom = msg

    # Detection callback

    def _on_detections(self, msg: ObstacleDetectionArray):
        updated = 0
        created = 0
        rejected = 0

        for det in msg.detections:
            world_pt = self._transform_to_map_frame(det.position, msg.header)
            if world_pt is None:
                continue  # transform failed — skip this detection

            wx, wy, wz = world_pt

            # 1. Associate with the nearest existing track (Mahalanobis gate).
            best = None
            best_d_sq = self._assoc_gate_sq
            for track in self._tracks:
                d_sq = track.mahalanobis_sq(wx, wy, wz, self._r_xy, self._r_z)
                if d_sq < best_d_sq:
                    best_d_sq = d_sq
                    best = track

            if best is not None:
                best.update(
                    wx, wy, wz,
                    det.dimensions.x, det.dimensions.y, det.dimensions.z,
                    self._r_xy, self._r_z,
                )
                updated += 1
                continue

            # 2. New obstacle — verify it against the trusted terrain before
            #    a track is born: its bbox bottom must sit on the base map.
            if not self._terrain_consistent(wx, wy, wz - det.dimensions.z / 2.0):
                rejected += 1
                continue

            self._tracks.append(
                _ObstacleTrack(
                    x=wx, y=wy, z=wz,
                    var_x=self._r_xy, var_y=self._r_xy, var_z=self._r_z,
                    dim_x=det.dimensions.x,
                    dim_y=det.dimensions.y,
                    dim_z=det.dimensions.z,
                    class_id=det.class_id,
                )
            )
            created += 1

        if updated or created:
            self._rebuild_height_map()

        if updated or created or rejected:
            self.get_logger().debug(
                f"Detections — track updates: {updated}  new tracks: {created}  "
                f"terrain-rejected: {rejected}  tracks total: {len(self._tracks)}"
            )

    def _terrain_consistent(self, wx: float, wy: float, bottom_z: float) -> bool:
        """Gate a prospective obstacle's bbox bottom against the trusted base
        terrain height at (wx, wy). Base cells carry initial_height_variance
        (tiny — the map is respected); unmapped NaN cells carry
        unknown_height_variance, which makes the gate pass automatically
        there. Out-of-grid detections are likewise unverifiable but allowed."""
        col = int((wx - self._origin_x) / self._resolution)
        row = int((wy - self._origin_y) / self._resolution)
        if not (0 <= row < self._rows and 0 <= col < self._cols):
            return True

        terrain = float(self._base_height_map[row, col])
        var_terrain = self._unknown_variance if np.isnan(terrain) else self._base_variance
        if np.isnan(terrain):
            terrain = 0.0

        innovation_sq = (bottom_z - terrain) ** 2
        return innovation_sq / (var_terrain + self._r_z) < self._terrain_gate_sq

    def _rebuild_height_map(self):
        """Recompute the published height map: the immutable base terrain
        plus every VERIFIED track's bbox top stamped over its footprint at
        the track's current filtered position. Rebuilding from scratch means
        a track whose estimate shifts cells between sightings never leaves a
        stale stamp behind."""
        hm = self._base_height_map.copy()
        for track in self._tracks:
            if track.mean_variance() > self._commit_variance:
                continue  # not yet verified — stays out of the published maps
            top = track.z + track.dim_z / 2.0
            for row, col in self._bbox_to_cells(track.x, track.y, track.dim_x, track.dim_y):
                hm[row, col] = np.fmax(hm[row, col], top)
        self._height_map = hm

# QoS — TRANSIENT_LOCAL so late-subscribing D* receives last message
        qos = QoSProfile(
            depth=1,
            durability=DurabilityPolicy.TRANSIENT_LOCAL,
            reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.RELIABLE
        )

        # Subscriptions — heightmap only (no /map needed)
        self.create_subscription(OccupancyGrid, self.hm_topic, self.hm_cb, qos)
        self.create_subscription(Float32MultiArray, self.hm_range_topic, self.range_cb, qos)

        # Publisher
        self.pub = self.create_publisher(OccupancyGrid, self.out_topic, qos)

        # Timer-based publish at configured rate
        self.timer = self.create_timer(1.0 / self.pub_rate, self.timer_cb)
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Unified Costmap Fuser ready (heightmap-only mode). "
            f"Subscribed to {self.hm_topic}, {self.hm_range_topic}. "
            f"Publishing on {self.out_topic} at {self.pub_rate} Hz. "
            f"Inflation: inscribed={self.inscribed_radius}m, "
            f"radius={self.inflation_radius}m, scaling={self.inflation_scaling}")

    def hm_cb(self, msg):
        self.latest_hm = msg

    def range_cb(self, msg):
        if len(msg.data) >= 2:
            self.hm_range = [msg.data[0], msg.data[1]]

    def timer_cb(self):
        if self.latest_hm is None:
            return

        start_time = time.time()
        hm_msg = self.latest_hm

        H_w = hm_msg.info.width
        H_h = hm_msg.info.height
        res = hm_msg.info.resolution

        if res <= 0:
            self.get_logger().warn("Invalid resolution in heightmap.")
            return

        # Validate data size
        if len(hm_msg.data) != H_w * H_h:
            self.get_logger().warn("Heightmap data size mismatch, skipping.")
            return

        # Log and cache when dimensions change
        if self.last_dims != (H_w, H_h):
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Heightmap grid: {H_w}x{H_h}, res={res:.3f}m.")
            self.last_dims = (H_w, H_h)
            self._cached_meshgrid = np.meshgrid(np.arange(H_w), np.arange(H_h))

        # ─── Step 1: Decode heightmap to meters ─────────────────────────
        hm_data = np.array(hm_msg.data, dtype=np.float32).reshape((H_h, H_w))
        valid_hm = (hm_data != -1)
        h_meters = np.zeros_like(hm_data, dtype=np.float32)

        if self.hm_range is not None:
            h_min, h_range = self.hm_range
            h_meters[valid_hm] = h_min + (hm_data[valid_hm] / 100.0) * h_range
        else:
            h_meters[valid_hm] = hm_data[valid_hm] * self.hm_scale

        # Guard against all-invalid heightmap (NaN poisoning)
        if np.any(valid_hm):
            h_meters[~valid_hm] = np.mean(h_meters[valid_hm])
        else:
            out_msg = OccupancyGrid()
            out_msg.header = hm_msg.header
            out_msg.info = hm_msg.info
            out_msg.data = [-1] * (H_w * H_h)
            self.pub.publish(out_msg)
            return

        # ─── Step 2: Compute terrain derivatives ────────────────────────
        h_blur = cv2.GaussianBlur(h_meters, (3, 3), 0)

        # 1st derivative (steepness) via Sobel
        sobel_x = cv2.Sobel(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0, ksize=3)
        sobel_y = cv2.Sobel(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1, ksize=3)
        steepness = np.sqrt(sobel_x ** 2 + sobel_y ** 2)

        # 2nd derivative (roughness) via Laplacian
        roughness = np.abs(cv2.Laplacian(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F))

        # Normalize to 0-99 (100 is reserved for lethal)
        norm_steep = np.clip((steepness / self.max_slope) * 99.0, 0, 99)
        norm_rough = np.clip((roughness / self.max_roughness) * 99.0, 0, 99)

        # Merge with configurable weights
        terrain_cost = np.clip(
            norm_steep * self.steep_w + norm_rough * self.rough_w, 0, 99)

        # ─── Step 3: Detect lethal cells from heightmap ─────────────────
        # Steep slopes → lethal
        steep_lethal = steepness > self.max_slope

        # Height diffs (cliffs) → lethal (3x3 max-min filter)
        kernel_3x3 = np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)
        max_h = cv2.dilate(h_blur, kernel_3x3)
        min_h = cv2.erode(h_blur, kernel_3x3)
        diff_lethal = (max_h - min_h) > self.max_h_diff

        lethal_mask = (steep_lethal | diff_lethal) & valid_hm

        # ─── Step 4: Inflation layer ────────────────────────────────────
        # Build binary lethal image for distance transform
        lethal_binary = lethal_mask.astype(np.uint8)  # 1 = lethal, 0 = free

        # Distance transform: compute distance from each cell to nearest lethal
        # cv2.distanceTransform needs inverted input (0 = obstacle)
        dist_map = cv2.distanceTransform(
            (1 - lethal_binary), cv2.DIST_L2, 5) * res  # convert to meters

        # Inscribed inflation: cells within inscribed_radius → also lethal
        inscribed_mask = dist_map < self.inscribed_radius

        # Gradual inflation: exponential decay between inscribed and inflation radius
        # inflation_cost = 99 * exp(-scaling * (dist - inscribed_radius) / (inflation_radius - inscribed_radius))
        inflation_cost = np.zeros_like(dist_map, dtype=np.float64)
        inflation_band = (dist_map >= self.inscribed_radius) & (dist_map < self.inflation_radius)
        if self.inflation_radius > self.inscribed_radius:
            normalized_dist = (dist_map[inflation_band] - self.inscribed_radius) / \
                              (self.inflation_radius - self.inscribed_radius)
            inflation_cost[inflation_band] = 99.0 * np.exp(-self.inflation_scaling * normalized_dist)

        # ─── Step 5: Combine everything ─────────────────────────────────
        # Start with terrain cost as base
        out = terrain_cost.copy()

        # Overlay inflation cost (take max of terrain and inflation)
        out = np.maximum(out, inflation_cost)

        # Mark lethal cells (original + inscribed inflation)
        all_lethal = lethal_mask | inscribed_mask
        out[all_lethal] = 100

        # Mark unknown cells
        hm_unknown = ~valid_hm
        out[hm_unknown] = -1

        # Clamp non-lethal, non-unknown to [0, 99]
        free_mask = ~all_lethal & valid_hm
        out[free_mask] = np.clip(out[free_mask], 0, 99)

        out = out.astype(np.int8)

        # ─── Step 6: Dilate unknown regions ─────────────────────────────
        unknown_mask = (out == -1).astype(np.uint8)
        if np.any(unknown_mask):
            dilated = cv2.dilate(unknown_mask, kernel_3x3, iterations=2).astype(bool)
            out[dilated] = -1

        # ─── Step 7: Publish ────────────────────────────────────────────
        out_msg = OccupancyGrid()
        out_msg.header = hm_msg.header
        out_msg.info = hm_msg.info
        out_msg.data = out.flatten().tolist()
        self.pub.publish(out_msg)

class ERCWaypointFollower(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('erc_waypoint_follower')
        self.client = ActionClient(self, NavigateToPose, 'navigate_to_pose')
        self.odom_sub = self.create_subscription(
            Odometry, '/odom', self.odom_callback, 10
        )
        self.current_pose = None

    def odom_callback(self, msg):
        self.current_pose = msg.pose.pose

    def navigate_to_waypoint(self, x, y):
        self.get_logger().info(f"\n---> Connecting to '/navigate_to_pose' Action Server...")
        if not self.client.wait_for_server(timeout_sec=120.0):
            self.get_logger().error("Action server '/navigate_to_pose' not available.")
            return False

        goal_msg = NavigateToPose.Goal()
        goal_msg.pose.header.frame_id = 'map'
        goal_msg.pose.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        goal_msg.pose.pose.position.x = x
        goal_msg.pose.pose.position.y = y
        goal_msg.pose.pose.orientation.w = 1.0

        self.get_logger().info(f"Sending waypoint goal: ({x:.2f}, {y:.2f})")
        send_goal_future = self.client.send_goal_async(goal_msg)
        
        # Wait for goal acceptance
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self, send_goal_future)
        goal_handle = send_goal_future.result()

        if not goal_handle.accepted:
            self.get_logger().error("Goal was rejected by the action server.")
            return False

        self.get_logger().info("Goal accepted. Moving to waypoint...")
        get_result_future = goal_handle.get_result_async()
        
        # Wait for execution result
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self, get_result_future)
        result = get_result_future.result()
        
        if result.status == GoalStatus.STATUS_SUCCEEDED:
            self.get_logger().info("Target waypoint reached!")
            if self.current_pose is not None:
                rx = self.current_pose.position.x
                ry = self.current_pose.position.y
                dist = math.hypot(rx - x, ry - y)

    def _clock_callback(self, msg: Clock):
        t = msg.clock.sec + (msg.clock.nanosec * 1e-9)
        if self.sim_start_time is None:
            self.sim_start_time = t
            self.last_clock_time = t
            self.total_waiting_time = 0.0

        if self.tracker.state.name == "WAITING_FOR_COMMAND":
            self.total_waiting_time += (t - self.last_clock_time)

        self.current_sim_time = (t - self.sim_start_time) - self.total_waiting_time
        self.last_clock_time = t

    def _command_callback(self, msg: String):
        cmd = msg.data.strip().upper()
        if cmd == "NEXT":
            if self.tracker.resume_mission():
                self.get_logger().info("Referee Command: NEXT -> Target updated.")
        elif cmd in ("SKIP", "FAIL"):
            curr_pose = (self.current_x, self.current_y)
            if self.tracker.skip_current_waypoint(self.current_sim_time, curr_pose):
                self.get_logger().info(f"Referee Command: {cmd} -> Current waypoint marked as FAILED and skipped.")
        elif cmd.startswith("WAYPOINT_RESULT:") or cmd.startswith("RESULT:"):
            try:
                parts = cmd.split(":")
                if len(parts) == 5:
                    wp_id = parts[1]
                    rx = float(parts[2])
                    ry = float(parts[3])
                    dist_err = float(parts[4])
                else:
                    wp_id = "LAST"
                    rx = float(parts[1])
                    ry = float(parts[2])
                    dist_err = float(parts[3])
                if self.tracker.override_waypoint_result(wp_id, rx, ry, dist_err):
                    self.get_logger().info(f"Referee Command: RESULT -> Updated waypoint '{wp_id}' result to pose ({rx:.2f}, {ry:.2f}) | Error: {dist_err:.3f}m")
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().warn(f"Failed to parse RESULT command {cmd}: {e}")
        elif cmd == "RETURN":
            self.tracker.record_return_request()
            self.get_logger().info(f"Referee Command: RETURN -> Return penalty registered ({self.tracker.num_returns} total).")
        elif cmd == "COLLISION":
            self.safety_engine.trigger_collision()

    def _pose_callback(self, msg: Odometry):
        if self.run_finished:
            return
        new_x = msg.pose.pose.position.x
        new_y = msg.pose.pose.position.y

        # Use the actual velocity from odometry twist (much more reliable than pose-delta)
        vx = msg.twist.twist.linear.x
        vy = msg.twist.twist.linear.y
        self.current_speed = math.hypot(vx, vy)

        self.current_x = new_x
        self.current_y = new_y

        self.safety_engine.check_boundary(msg.pose.pose)
        self.tracker.update_position(
            (self.current_x, self.current_y),
            self.current_sim_time,
            self.current_speed
        )

    def _collision_callback(self, msg: Bool):
        if self.run_finished:
            return
        if msg.data:
            self.safety_engine.trigger_collision()

    def _save_summary_file(self, result_dict):
        """Helper to continuously persist run_summary.npy so it is never missing."""
        try:
            summary_array = np.array(result_dict, dtype=object)
            np.save(self.output_summary_path, summary_array)
            # Also save to fixed reports directory as a reliable fallback
            ws_root = os.environ.get('ROAR_WS', str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]))
            fixed_reports_dir = os.path.join(ws_root, 'reports', 'referee')
            os.makedirs(fixed_reports_dir, exist_ok=True)
            np.save(os.path.join(fixed_reports_dir, 'run_summary.npy'), summary_array)
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().warn(f"Failed to write summary file: {e}")

    def _evaluation_loop(self):
        if self.run_finished:
            return

        waypoints_remaining = len(self.tracker.waypoints) - self.tracker.waypoints_completed
        is_completed = (self.tracker.state.name == "COMPLETED")

        status, msg_log, is_fatal = self.safety_engine.evaluate_terminal_state(
            self.current_x,
            self.current_y,
            self.current_sim_time,
            waypoints_remaining,
            is_completed=is_completed
        )

        # Periodically compute current score and persist summary
        score_dict = self.score_engine.final_score(
            waypoint_details=self.tracker.waypoint_records,
            back_to_start_detail=self.tracker.back_to_start_record,
            num_return_requests=self.tracker.num_returns,
            only_gnss_used=self.only_gnss_used,
            elapsed_time=self.current_sim_time,
            is_fatal=is_fatal
        )
        score_dict["terminal_status"] = status
        score_dict["is_final"] = is_completed or is_fatal or (status in ["KILL", "TIMEOUT", "SUCCESS"])
        score_dict["t_min_computed_sec"] = float(self.t_min_computed)
        score_dict["t_max_computed_sec"] = float(self.t_max_computed)
        score_dict["minimum_time_sec"] = float(self.minimum_time)
        score_dict["maximum_time_sec"] = float(self.maximum_time)
        score_dict["ideal_distance_m"] = float(self.total_ideal_distance)
        score_dict["actual_distance_m"] = float(self.tracker.actual_distance)

        # Save summary continuously so file exists at all times
        self._save_summary_file(score_dict)

            self._conclude_run(status=status, is_fatal=is_fatal)
            return

        score_msg.data = json.dumps(score_dict)

def listener_callback(self, msg: PointCloud2):
        # Read all params fresh each call → ros2 param set takes effect live
        p = self._read_params()

        # ── Stage 0: GPU-accelerated ROI distance mask ───────────────────
        points, colors = self._pc2_to_numpy_rgb(msg)
        if points.shape[0] == 0:
            return

        if self._use_gpu:
            # Upload to GPU, compute squared norms, threshold, download mask
            pts_t  = o3c.Tensor(points, dtype=o3c.float32, device=self._gpu_device)
            sq     = (pts_t * pts_t).sum(1)                     # Nx1 squared distances
            mask_t = sq < float(p['max_dist'] ** 2)             # boolean mask on GPU
            mask   = mask_t.cpu().numpy().astype(bool)
        else:
            mask = np.linalg.norm(points, axis=1) < p['max_dist']

        points = points[mask]
        colors = colors[mask]
        if points.shape[0] == 0:
            return

        # Wrap in Open3D legacy PointCloud for the rest of the pipeline
        pcd = o3d.geometry.PointCloud()
        pcd.points = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(points)
        pcd.colors = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(colors)

        # ── Stage 1: Voxel-grid downsampling ────────────────────────────
        pcd = pcd.voxel_down_sample(voxel_size=p['voxel_size'])
        if len(pcd.points) < 10:
            return

        # ── Stage 2: Statistical Outlier Removal (SOR) ──────────────────
        # Removes per-point speckle by comparing each point's mean
        # neighbour distance to the global mean±σ across all points.
        if p['sor_en'] and len(pcd.points) >= p['sor_k']:
            pcd, _ = pcd.remove_statistical_outlier(
                nb_neighbors=int(p['sor_k']),
                std_ratio=float(p['sor_std'])
            )
            if len(pcd.points) < 5:
                return

        # ── Stage 3: Radius Outlier Removal (ROR) ───────────────────────
        # Removes isolated points (sensor reflections) that survive SOR.
        if p['ror_en'] and len(pcd.points) >= p['ror_n']:
            pcd, _ = pcd.remove_radius_outlier(
                nb_points=int(p['ror_n']),
                radius=float(p['ror_r'])
            )
            if len(pcd.points) < 5:
                return

        # Publish clean cloud (with ground, for debugging in RViz)
        self.filtered_pub.publish(self._pcd_to_pc2_rgb(pcd, msg.header))

        # ── Stage 4: Slope-aware iterative RANSAC plane removal ─────────
        # Strips ground + ramps while PRESERVING steep rock faces.
        pcd_ng = self._remove_planes_slope_aware(pcd, p)
        if pcd_ng is None or len(pcd_ng.points) == 0:
            return

        # ── Stage 4b: Surface-normal roughness filter ────────────────────
        # Removes any remaining smooth-slope points; keeps only rough/sharp rock points.
        if p['roughness_en']:
            pcd_ng = self._roughness_filter(pcd_ng, p)
            if pcd_ng is None or len(pcd_ng.points) < 5:
                return

        self.no_ground_pub.publish(self._pcd_to_pc2_rgb(pcd_ng, msg.header))

        # ── Stage 5: DBSCAN clustering ───────────────────────────────────
        # Groups surviving points into candidate obstacle clusters.
        labels = np.array(
            pcd_ng.cluster_dbscan(
                eps=p['cluster_tol'],
                min_points=p['min_cluster'],
                print_progress=False
            )
        )

        # Build message containers
        detections     = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        raw_detections = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        slam_detections = ObstacleDetectionArray(header=msg.header)

        max_label = int(labels.max()) if labels.size > 0 else -1

        for i in range(max_label + 1):
            idx = np.where(labels == i)[0]
            if len(idx) < p['min_cluster'] or len(idx) > p['max_cluster']:
                continue  # DBSCAN already filters by min, but max is our extra gate

            cluster_pcd = pcd_ng.select_by_index(idx)
            aabb   = cluster_pcd.get_axis_aligned_bounding_box()
            center = aabb.get_center()
            extent = aabb.get_extent()
            sx, sy, sz = float(extent[0]), float(extent[1]), float(extent[2])
            cx, cy, cz = float(center[0]), float(center[1]), float(center[2])

            # Assemble Detection3D (shared by raw + filtered arrays)
            det = self._make_detection3d(msg.header, center, extent, i)
            raw_detections.detections.append(det)

            # ── Stage 6: Bounding-box shape filter ──────────────────────
            if not (p['min_bx'] <= sx <= p['max_bx'] and
                    p['min_by'] <= sy <= p['max_by'] and
                    p['min_bz'] <= sz <= p['max_bz']):
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by bbox: x={sx:.2f} y={sy:.2f} z={sz:.2f}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Aspect-ratio filter (flat slab rejection) ───────
            # A ramp remnant is wide+deep but not tall.  Rocks are chunkier.
            if p['max_dr'] > 0 and sy > 1e-3 and (sz / sy) > p['max_dr']:
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by depth/height={sz/sy:.1f} > {p["max_dr"]}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Distance filter ─────────────────────────────────
            cl_dist = float(np.linalg.norm([cx, cy, cz]))
            if cl_dist < p['min_cdist'] or cl_dist > p['max_cdist']:
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Centre-height (Y-axis) filter ───────────────────
            # ZED Y=down; positive Y = below camera (on ground level).
            # Rocks sit near Y=0..+0.5; reject clusters above or far below.
            if cy < p['min_cy'] or cy > p['max_cy']:
                continue

            detections.detections.append(det)

            # Build SLAM-format obstacle
            slam_obs = ObstacleDetection()
            slam_obs.position   = Point(x=cx, y=cy, z=cz)
            slam_obs.dimensions = Vector3(x=sx, y=sy, z=sz)
            slam_detections.detections.append(slam_obs)

        # Publish
        self.raw_cluster_pub.publish(raw_detections)
        self.cluster_pub.publish(detections)
        self.slam_pub.publish(slam_detections)
        self._publish_markers(detections, msg.header)

def hm_cb(self, msg):
        self.latest_hm = msg

    def range_cb(self, msg):
        if len(msg.data) >= 2:
            self.hm_range = [msg.data[0], msg.data[1]]

    def timer_cb(self):
        if self.latest_hm is None:
            return

        start_time = time.time()
        hm_msg = self.latest_hm

        H_w = hm_msg.info.width
        H_h = hm_msg.info.height
        res = hm_msg.info.resolution

        if res <= 0:
            self.get_logger().warn("Invalid resolution in heightmap.")
            return

        # Validate data size
        if len(hm_msg.data) != H_w * H_h:
            self.get_logger().warn("Heightmap data size mismatch, skipping.")
            return

        # Log and cache when dimensions change
        if self.last_dims != (H_w, H_h):
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Heightmap grid: {H_w}x{H_h}, res={res:.3f}m.")
            self.last_dims = (H_w, H_h)
            self._cached_meshgrid = np.meshgrid(np.arange(H_w), np.arange(H_h))

        # ─── Step 1: Decode heightmap to meters ─────────────────────────
        hm_data = np.array(hm_msg.data, dtype=np.float32).reshape((H_h, H_w))
        valid_hm = (hm_data != -1)
        h_meters = np.zeros_like(hm_data, dtype=np.float32)

        if self.hm_range is not None:
            h_min, h_range = self.hm_range
            h_meters[valid_hm] = h_min + (hm_data[valid_hm] / 100.0) * h_range
        else:
            h_meters[valid_hm] = hm_data[valid_hm] * self.hm_scale

        # Guard against all-invalid heightmap (NaN poisoning)
        if np.any(valid_hm):
            h_meters[~valid_hm] = np.mean(h_meters[valid_hm])
        else:
            out_msg = OccupancyGrid()
            out_msg.header = hm_msg.header
            out_msg.info = hm_msg.info
            out_msg.data = [-1] * (H_w * H_h)
            self.pub.publish(out_msg)
            return

        # ─── Step 2: Compute terrain derivatives ────────────────────────
        h_blur = cv2.GaussianBlur(h_meters, (3, 3), 0)

        # 1st derivative (steepness) via Sobel
        sobel_x = cv2.Sobel(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F, 1, 0, ksize=3)
        sobel_y = cv2.Sobel(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F, 0, 1, ksize=3)
        steepness = np.sqrt(sobel_x ** 2 + sobel_y ** 2)

        # 2nd derivative (roughness) via Laplacian
        roughness = np.abs(cv2.Laplacian(h_blur, cv2.CV_32F))

        # Normalize to 0-99 (100 is reserved for lethal)
        norm_steep = np.clip((steepness / self.max_slope) * 99.0, 0, 99)
        norm_rough = np.clip((roughness / self.max_roughness) * 99.0, 0, 99)

        # Merge with configurable weights
        terrain_cost = np.clip(
            norm_steep * self.steep_w + norm_rough * self.rough_w, 0, 99)

        # ─── Step 3: Detect lethal cells from heightmap ─────────────────
        # Steep slopes → lethal
        steep_lethal = steepness > self.max_slope

        # Height diffs (cliffs) → lethal (3x3 max-min filter)
        kernel_3x3 = np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8)
        max_h = cv2.dilate(h_blur, kernel_3x3)
        min_h = cv2.erode(h_blur, kernel_3x3)
        diff_lethal = (max_h - min_h) > self.max_h_diff

        lethal_mask = (steep_lethal | diff_lethal) & valid_hm

        # ─── Step 4: Inflation layer ────────────────────────────────────
        # Build binary lethal image for distance transform
        lethal_binary = lethal_mask.astype(np.uint8)  # 1 = lethal, 0 = free

        # Distance transform: compute distance from each cell to nearest lethal
        # cv2.distanceTransform needs inverted input (0 = obstacle)
        dist_map = cv2.distanceTransform(
            (1 - lethal_binary), cv2.DIST_L2, 5) * res  # convert to meters

        # Inscribed inflation: cells within inscribed_radius → also lethal
        inscribed_mask = dist_map < self.inscribed_radius

        # Gradual inflation: exponential decay between inscribed and inflation radius
        # inflation_cost = 99 * exp(-scaling * (dist - inscribed_radius) / (inflation_radius - inscribed_radius))
        inflation_cost = np.zeros_like(dist_map, dtype=np.float64)
        inflation_band = (dist_map >= self.inscribed_radius) & (dist_map < self.inflation_radius)
        if self.inflation_radius > self.inscribed_radius:
            normalized_dist = (dist_map[inflation_band] - self.inscribed_radius) / \
                              (self.inflation_radius - self.inscribed_radius)
            inflation_cost[inflation_band] = 99.0 * np.exp(-self.inflation_scaling * normalized_dist)

        # ─── Step 5: Combine everything ─────────────────────────────────
        # Start with terrain cost as base
        out = terrain_cost.copy()

        # Overlay inflation cost (take max of terrain and inflation)
        out = np.maximum(out, inflation_cost)

        # Mark lethal cells (original + inscribed inflation)
        all_lethal = lethal_mask | inscribed_mask
        out[all_lethal] = 100

        # Mark unknown cells
        hm_unknown = ~valid_hm
        out[hm_unknown] = -1

        # Clamp non-lethal, non-unknown to [0, 99]
        free_mask = ~all_lethal & valid_hm
        out[free_mask] = np.clip(out[free_mask], 0, 99)

        out = out.astype(np.int8)

        # ─── Step 6: Dilate unknown regions ─────────────────────────────
        unknown_mask = (out == -1).astype(np.uint8)
        if np.any(unknown_mask):
            dilated = cv2.dilate(unknown_mask, kernel_3x3, iterations=2).astype(bool)
            out[dilated] = -1

        # ─── Step 7: Publish ────────────────────────────────────────────
        out_msg = OccupancyGrid()
        out_msg.header = hm_msg.header
        out_msg.info = hm_msg.info
        out_msg.data = out.flatten().tolist()
        self.pub.publish(out_msg)

def navigate_to_waypoint(self, x, y):
        self.get_logger().info(f"\n---> Connecting to '/navigate_to_pose' Action Server...")
        if not self.client.wait_for_server(timeout_sec=120.0):
            self.get_logger().error("Action server '/navigate_to_pose' not available.")
            return False

        goal_msg = NavigateToPose.Goal()
        goal_msg.pose.header.frame_id = 'map'
        goal_msg.pose.header.stamp = self.get_clock().now().to_msg()
        goal_msg.pose.pose.position.x = x
        goal_msg.pose.pose.position.y = y
        goal_msg.pose.pose.orientation.w = 1.0

        self.get_logger().info(f"Sending waypoint goal: ({x:.2f}, {y:.2f})")
        send_goal_future = self.client.send_goal_async(goal_msg)
        
        # Wait for goal acceptance
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self, send_goal_future)
        goal_handle = send_goal_future.result()

        if not goal_handle.accepted:
            self.get_logger().error("Goal was rejected by the action server.")
            return False

        self.get_logger().info("Goal accepted. Moving to waypoint...")
        get_result_future = goal_handle.get_result_async()
        
        # Wait for execution result
        rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(self, get_result_future)
        result = get_result_future.result()

def contact_callback(self, msg: Contacts):
        if not msg.contacts:
            return

        for contact in msg.contacts:
            c1 = contact.collision1.name
            c2 = contact.collision2.name
            
            # Find the obstacle name (e.g., "Rock_5::link::collision")
            obstacle_name = c2 if "roar_rover" in c1 else c1
            
            if "Rock_" in obstacle_name:
                # Extract the base entity name (e.g., "Rock_5")
                entity_name = obstacle_name.split("::")[0]
                
                # Look up the mesh_id for this entity
                mesh_id = self.entity_to_mesh.get(entity_name, -1)
                
                if mesh_id in self.safe_meshes:
                    # It's one of the non-collidable meshes (4,5,6,7,9), ignore it!
                    continue

            # If we get here, it's a valid fatal collision (collidable rock, wall, etc.)
            self.is_colliding = True
            self.last_contact_time = self.get_clock().now()
            
            flag_msg = Bool()
            flag_msg.data = True
            self.pub.publish(flag_msg)
            return  # Trigger alarm immediately

def _evaluation_loop(self):
        if self.run_finished:
            return

        waypoints_remaining = len(self.tracker.waypoints) - self.tracker.waypoints_completed
        is_completed = (self.tracker.state.name == "COMPLETED")

        status, msg_log, is_fatal = self.safety_engine.evaluate_terminal_state(
            self.current_x,
            self.current_y,
            self.current_sim_time,
            waypoints_remaining,
            is_completed=is_completed
        )

        # Periodically compute current score and persist summary
        score_dict = self.score_engine.final_score(
            waypoint_details=self.tracker.waypoint_records,
            back_to_start_detail=self.tracker.back_to_start_record,
            num_return_requests=self.tracker.num_returns,
            only_gnss_used=self.only_gnss_used,
            elapsed_time=self.current_sim_time,
            is_fatal=is_fatal
        )
        score_dict["terminal_status"] = status
        score_dict["is_final"] = is_completed or is_fatal or (status in ["KILL", "TIMEOUT", "SUCCESS"])
        score_dict["t_min_computed_sec"] = float(self.t_min_computed)
        score_dict["t_max_computed_sec"] = float(self.t_max_computed)
        score_dict["minimum_time_sec"] = float(self.minimum_time)
        score_dict["maximum_time_sec"] = float(self.maximum_time)
        score_dict["ideal_distance_m"] = float(self.total_ideal_distance)
        score_dict["actual_distance_m"] = float(self.tracker.actual_distance)

        # Save summary continuously so file exists at all times
        self._save_summary_file(score_dict)

        if is_fatal or status in ["KILL", "TIMEOUT", "SUCCESS"] or is_completed:
            self._conclude_run(status=status, is_fatal=is_fatal)
            return

        score_msg = String()
        score_msg.data = json.dumps(score_dict)
        self.score_pub.publish(score_msg)

        status_msg = String()
        status_str = "WAITING FOR COMMAND" if self.tracker.state.name == "WAITING_FOR_COMMAND" else "RUNNING"
        status_msg.data = f"{status_str} | Waypoints: {self.tracker.waypoints_completed}/{len(self.tracker.waypoints)}"
        self.status_pub.publish(status_msg)

def rgb_callback(self, rgb_msg: Image):
        try:
            cv_rgb = self.bridge.imgmsg_to_cv2(rgb_msg, desired_encoding='bgr8').copy()
            h, w, _ = cv_rgb.shape

            # Mars atmospheric dust speckle
            dust_probs = np.random.uniform(0.0, 1.0, size=(h, w))
            dust_mask = dust_probs < 0.015
            cv_rgb[dust_mask] = np.array([80, 120, 180], dtype=np.uint8)

            u, v = self.get_sun_pixel()

            if u is not None and v is not None:
                glare_radius = 150.0

                    dist_from_sun = np.sqrt((X - u) ** 2 + (Y - v) ** 2)

                    norm_dist = np.clip(1.0 - (dist_from_sun / glare_radius), 0.0, 1.0)
                    core = (norm_dist ** 2.5)[..., np.newaxis]
                    corona = (norm_dist ** 1.4)[..., np.newaxis]

                    # Bright white solar core + warm golden-white lens corona (BGR)
                    bloom = (
                        core * np.array([255.0, 255.0, 255.0], dtype=np.float32)
                        + corona * np.array([90.0, 190.0, 255.0], dtype=np.float32) * 0.65

def _remove_planes_slope_aware(self, pcd, p) -> o3d.geometry.PointCloud:
        """
        Iteratively finds and removes dominant planes, but ONLY if the plane:
          (a) has >= plane_min_inliers points (small planes = rock faces → keep)
          (b) its normal tilts <= ground_max_tilt_deg from vertical (ZED Y axis)
              → near-vertical walls / rock faces are NEVER removed
          (c) its centroid depth (Z) is within [gnd_min_z, gnd_max_z]
              → prevents accidentally removing a floating rock cluster

        This is the key improvement over the old all-planes-stripped approach:
        a ramp at 30° is removed; a near-vertical boulder face at 80° is kept.
        """
        cos_limit = math.cos(math.radians(float(p['gnd_tilt'])))
        current   = pcd

        for i in range(int(p['plane_iters'])):
            if len(current.points) < 20:
                break

            try:
                plane_model, inliers = current.segment_plane(
                    distance_threshold=float(p['gnd_thresh']),
                    ransac_n=3,
                    num_iterations=200
                )
            except Exception:
                break

            if len(inliers) < int(p['plane_inliers']):
                # Too few inliers → this is a small feature (rock), not ground. Stop.
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'RANSAC iter {i}: {len(inliers)} inliers < {p["plane_inliers"]}, stopping.'
                )
                break

            # Compute cosine between plane normal and gravity (Y axis)
            normal = np.array(plane_model[:3], dtype=np.float64)
            normal /= np.linalg.norm(normal) + 1e-9
            cos_with_gravity = abs(float(np.dot(normal, _GRAVITY)))

            # Compute centroid depth (Z = forward in ZED frame)
            pts_arr = np.asarray(current.points)
            centroid_z = float(np.mean(pts_arr[inliers, 2]))

            # Check centroid depth is in valid ground range
            depth_ok = p['gnd_min_z'] <= centroid_z <= p['gnd_max_z']

            # Remove the plane only if it is "ground-like"
            if cos_with_gravity >= cos_limit and depth_ok:
                axis = ['X', 'Y', 'Z'][int(np.argmax(np.abs(normal)))]
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'RANSAC iter {i}: removed {len(inliers)} pts  '
                    f'normal≈{normal.round(2)}  dominant={axis}  '
                    f'tilt_ok  centroid_z={centroid_z:.2f}'
                )
                current = current.select_by_index(inliers, invert=True)
            else:
                # This plane is too steep (rock face) or at wrong depth — stop.
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'RANSAC iter {i}: KEPT {len(inliers)} pts  '
                    f'cos_grav={cos_with_gravity:.2f} < {cos_limit:.2f} '
                    f'or depth_ok={depth_ok}. Stopping.'
                )
                break

        return current

    def _roughness_filter(self, pcd, p) -> o3d.geometry.PointCloud:
        """
        Computes surface normals for every point and measures local roughness
        (curvature / normal variance) in the neighbourhood.

        Algorithm:
          1. Estimate normals using PCA in a sphere of radius normal_search_radius.
          2. For each point i, gather its neighbours within the same radius.
          3. Compute the mean normal of those neighbours.
          4. Roughness score = mean angular deviation of neighbours from the mean normal.
             High score → points are on a sharp edge or irregular surface (ROCK).
             Low score  → points are on a flat/smooth surface (SLOPE/GROUND).
          5. Drop points with roughness < min_roughness_score.

        GPU acceleration: step 1 (normal estimation) uses open3d.core CUDA
        tensors when use_gpu=true; steps 2-5 use NumPy on CPU (normal variance
        computation is memory-bound, not compute-bound, so CPU is adequate).
        """
        if len(pcd.points) < 10:
            return pcd

        radius = float(p['norm_radius'])
        thresh = float(p['roughness'])

        if self._use_gpu:
            # Estimate normals on GPU via the Tensor API, then bring back to CPU
            try:
                pcd_t = o3d.t.geometry.PointCloud.from_legacy(pcd)
                pcd_t = pcd_t.to(self._gpu_device)
                pcd_t.estimate_normals(
                    o3d.core.SizeVector([0, 30]),          # min 0, max 30 neighbours
                    radius=radius
                )
                normals = pcd_t.point.normals.cpu().numpy()
            except Exception:
                # GPU path failed (geometry API unstable) → fall back to CPU
                pcd.estimate_normals(
                    search_param=o3d.geometry.KDTreeSearchParamRadius(radius)
                )
                normals = np.asarray(pcd.normals)
        else:
            pcd.estimate_normals(
                search_param=o3d.geometry.KDTreeSearchParamRadius(radius)
            )
            normals = np.asarray(pcd.normals)

        if normals.shape[0] == 0:
            return pcd

        # Normalise (PCA can return non-unit normals in edge cases)
        norms_len = np.linalg.norm(normals, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-9
        normals  /= norms_len

        # Build KD-tree on CPU for neighbourhood queries
        pts_arr = np.asarray(pcd.points)
        kdtree  = o3d.geometry.KDTreeFlann(pcd)

        roughness_scores = np.zeros(len(pts_arr), dtype=np.float32)

        for j in range(len(pts_arr)):
            [k, nb_idx, _] = kdtree.search_radius_vector_3d(pts_arr[j], radius)
            if k < 3:

                roughness_scores[j] = 1.0

            mean_normal /= mn_len

            dots         = np.clip(nb_normals @ mean_normal, -1.0, 1.0)

            roughness_scores[j] = float(1.0 - np.mean(np.abs(dots)))

        # Keep only points that are rough enough to be obstacles
        keep_mask = roughness_scores >= thresh

            return pcd  # fallback: keep all (avoid empty cloud)

        return pcd.select_by_index(np.where(keep_mask)[0])

        # Groups surviving points into candidate obstacle clusters.
        labels = np.array(
            pcd_ng.cluster_dbscan(
                eps=p['cluster_tol'],
                min_points=p['min_cluster'],
                print_progress=False
            )
        )

        # Build message containers
        detections     = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        raw_detections = Detection3DArray(header=msg.header)
        slam_detections = ObstacleDetectionArray(header=msg.header)

        max_label = int(labels.max()) if labels.size > 0 else -1

        for i in range(max_label + 1):
            idx = np.where(labels == i)[0]
            if len(idx) < p['min_cluster'] or len(idx) > p['max_cluster']:
                continue  # DBSCAN already filters by min, but max is our extra gate

            cluster_pcd = pcd_ng.select_by_index(idx)
            aabb   = cluster_pcd.get_axis_aligned_bounding_box()
            center = aabb.get_center()
            extent = aabb.get_extent()
            sx, sy, sz = float(extent[0]), float(extent[1]), float(extent[2])
            cx, cy, cz = float(center[0]), float(center[1]), float(center[2])

            # Assemble Detection3D (shared by raw + filtered arrays)
            det = self._make_detection3d(msg.header, center, extent, i)
            raw_detections.detections.append(det)

            # ── Stage 6: Bounding-box shape filter ──────────────────────
            if not (p['min_bx'] <= sx <= p['max_bx'] and
                    p['min_by'] <= sy <= p['max_by'] and
                    p['min_bz'] <= sz <= p['max_bz']):
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by bbox: x={sx:.2f} y={sy:.2f} z={sz:.2f}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Aspect-ratio filter (flat slab rejection) ───────
            # A ramp remnant is wide+deep but not tall.  Rocks are chunkier.
            if p['max_dr'] > 0 and sy > 1e-3 and (sz / sy) > p['max_dr']:
                self.get_logger().debug(
                    f'Cluster {i} rejected by depth/height={sz/sy:.1f} > {p["max_dr"]}'
                )
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Distance filter ─────────────────────────────────
            cl_dist = float(np.linalg.norm([cx, cy, cz]))
            if cl_dist < p['min_cdist'] or cl_dist > p['max_cdist']:
                continue

            # ── Stage 6: Centre-height (Y-axis) filter ───────────────────
            # ZED Y=down; positive Y = below camera (on ground level).
            # Rocks sit near Y=0..+0.5; reject clusters above or far below.
            if cy < p['min_cy'] or cy > p['max_cy']:
                continue

detections.detections.append(det)

            # Build SLAM-format obstacle
            slam_obs = ObstacleDetection()
            slam_obs.position   = Point(x=cx, y=cy, z=cz)
            slam_obs.dimensions = Vector3(x=sx, y=sy, z=sz)
            slam_detections.detections.append(slam_obs)

        # Publish
        self.raw_cluster_pub.publish(raw_detections)
        self.cluster_pub.publish(detections)
        self.slam_pub.publish(slam_detections)
        self._publish_markers(detections, msg.header)

def callback(self, msg: Detection3DArray):
        max_base_h   = self.get_parameter('max_obstacle_base_height').value
        min_conf     = self.get_parameter('min_confidence').value
        source_frame = self.get_parameter('source_frame').value
        merge_radius = self.get_parameter('merge_radius').value
        ema_alpha    = self.get_parameter('ema_alpha').value

        world_frame  = self.get_parameter('world_frame').value

        # Use native TF2 to perfectly resolve the 6-frame tree offsets
        try:
            tf_stamped = self.tf_buffer.lookup_transform(
                world_frame,   # target frame
                source_frame,  # source frame (where the detections are)
                rclpy.time.Time(), # get the latest available
                timeout=rclpy.duration.Duration(seconds=0.2)
            )
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f'Waiting for TF tree to link {source_frame} to {world_frame}...',
                throttle_duration_sec=5.0,
            )
            return

        now = time.time()
        self.latest_stamp = msg.header.stamp

        for det in msg.detections:
            # Confidence filter (min_conf=0.0 by default — accept all LiDAR clusters)
            score    = det.results[0].hypothesis.score    if det.results else 1.0
            class_id = det.results[0].hypothesis.class_id if det.results else 'obstacle'
            if score < min_conf:
                continue

            # Height filter — evaluated in camera frame (Z is UP)
            bottom_z_cam = det.bbox.center.position.z - det.bbox.size.z / 2.0
            if bottom_z_cam > max_base_h:
                continue

            # Distance filter — 3D distance from camera origin in camera frame
            cx = det.bbox.center.position.x
            cy = det.bbox.center.position.y
            cz = det.bbox.center.position.z
            dist_cam = math.sqrt(cx*cx + cy*cy + cz*cz)
            if dist_cam > self.get_parameter('max_detection_distance').value:
                continue

            # Transform obstacle centre to world frame
            pt_cam        = PointStamped()
            pt_cam.header = msg.header
            pt_cam.point  = det.bbox.center.position
            try:
                pt_world = tf2_geometry_msgs.do_transform_point(pt_cam, tf_stamped)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().warn(f'Transform failed: {e}')
                continue

            # Build world-frame detection
            out_det = Detection3D()
            out_det.header.frame_id       = world_frame
            out_det.header.stamp          = msg.header.stamp
            out_det.bbox.center.position.x = pt_world.point.x
            out_det.bbox.center.position.y = pt_world.point.y
            out_det.bbox.center.position.z = pt_world.point.z
            out_det.bbox.center.orientation.w = 1.0
            out_det.bbox.size.x = det.bbox.size.x
            out_det.bbox.size.y = det.bbox.size.y
            out_det.bbox.size.z = det.bbox.size.z
            hyp = ObjectHypothesisWithPose()
            hyp.hypothesis.class_id = class_id
            hyp.hypothesis.score    = score
            out_det.results.append(hyp)

            # Merge into obstacle map: if a known obstacle is within merge_radius, update it;
            # otherwise add a new entry
            merged = False
            for entry in self.obstacle_map.values():
                existing = entry['detection']
                dx = existing.bbox.center.position.x - pt_world.point.x
                dy = existing.bbox.center.position.y - pt_world.point.y
                dz = existing.bbox.center.position.z - pt_world.point.z
                if math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz) < merge_radius:
                    # Update in place with EMA (Exponential Moving Average) to eliminate jitter
                    existing.bbox.center.position.x = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.x + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.x
                    existing.bbox.center.position.y = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.y + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.y
                    existing.bbox.center.position.z = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.center.position.z + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.center.position.z
                    
                    existing.bbox.size.x = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.x + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.x
                    existing.bbox.size.y = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.y + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.y
                    existing.bbox.size.z = (1 - ema_alpha) * existing.bbox.size.z + ema_alpha * out_det.bbox.size.z
                    
                    # Keep highest confidence score
                    if out_det.results and existing.results:
                        existing.results[0].hypothesis.score = max(existing.results[0].hypothesis.score, out_det.results[0].hypothesis.score)

                    entry['last_seen']  = now
                    merged = True
                    break

            if not merged:
                if len(self.obstacle_map) >= self.get_parameter('max_obstacles').value:
                    # Map is full — drop the lowest-confidence entry to make room
                    oldest_key = min(
                        self.obstacle_map,
                        key=lambda k: self.obstacle_map[k]['detection'].results[0].hypothesis.score
                        if self.obstacle_map[k]['detection'].results else 0.0
                    )
                    del self.obstacle_map[oldest_key]

                self.obstacle_map[self._next_id] = {
                    'detection':  out_det,
                    'last_seen':  now,
                    'color_idx':  self._next_id,  # fixed forever — colour won't change
                }
                self._next_id += 1

        # Forget stale obstacles
        self._forget_old(now)

    # ── Periodic publisher ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _publish_map(self):
        """Called by timer — publishes the full accumulated obstacle array."""

def _on_detections(self, msg: ObstacleDetectionArray):
        updated = 0
        created = 0
        rejected = 0

        for det in msg.detections:
            world_pt = self._transform_to_map_frame(det.position, msg.header)
            if world_pt is None:
                continue  # transform failed — skip this detection

            wx, wy, wz = world_pt

            # 1. Associate with the nearest existing track (Mahalanobis gate).
            best = None
            best_d_sq = self._assoc_gate_sq
            for track in self._tracks:
                d_sq = track.mahalanobis_sq(wx, wy, wz, self._r_xy, self._r_z)
                if d_sq < best_d_sq:
                    best_d_sq = d_sq
                    best = track

            if best is not None:
                best.update(
                    wx, wy, wz,
                    det.dimensions.x, det.dimensions.y, det.dimensions.z,
                    self._r_xy, self._r_z,
                )
                updated += 1
                continue

            # 2. New obstacle — verify it against the trusted terrain before
            #    a track is born: its bbox bottom must sit on the base map.
            if not self._terrain_consistent(wx, wy, wz - det.dimensions.z / 2.0):
                rejected += 1
                continue

            self._tracks.append(
                _ObstacleTrack(
                    x=wx, y=wy, z=wz,
                    var_x=self._r_xy, var_y=self._r_xy, var_z=self._r_z,
                    dim_x=det.dimensions.x,
                    dim_y=det.dimensions.y,
                    dim_z=det.dimensions.z,
                    class_id=det.class_id,
                )
            )
            created += 1

        if updated or created:
            self._rebuild_height_map()

        if updated or created or rejected:
            self.get_logger().debug(
                f"Detections — track updates: {updated}  new tracks: {created}  "
                f"terrain-rejected: {rejected}  tracks total: {len(self._tracks)}"
            )

    def _terrain_consistent(self, wx: float, wy: float, bottom_z: float) -> bool:
        """Gate a prospective obstacle's bbox bottom against the trusted base
        terrain height at (wx, wy). Base cells carry initial_height_variance
        (tiny — the map is respected); unmapped NaN cells carry
        unknown_height_variance, which makes the gate pass automatically
        there. Out-of-grid detections are likewise unverifiable but allowed."""
        col = int((wx - self._origin_x) / self._resolution)
        row = int((wy - self._origin_y) / self._resolution)
        if not (0 <= row < self._rows and 0 <= col < self._cols):
            return True

        terrain = float(self._base_height_map[row, col])
        var_terrain = self._unknown_variance if np.isnan(terrain) else self._base_variance
        if np.isnan(terrain):
            terrain = 0.0

        innovation_sq = (bottom_z - terrain) ** 2
        return innovation_sq / (var_terrain + self._r_z) < self._terrain_gate_sq

    def _rebuild_height_map(self):
        """Recompute the published height map: the immutable base terrain
        plus every VERIFIED track's bbox top stamped over its footprint at
        the track's current filtered position. Rebuilding from scratch means
        a track whose estimate shifts cells between sightings never leaves a
        stale stamp behind."""
        hm = self._base_height_map.copy()
        for track in self._tracks:
            if track.mean_variance() > self._commit_variance:
                continue  # not yet verified — stays out of the published maps
            top = track.z + track.dim_z / 2.0
            for row, col in self._bbox_to_cells(track.x, track.y, track.dim_x, track.dim_y):
                hm[row, col] = np.fmax(hm[row, col], top)
        self._height_map = hm
